subject: Sector sync: partner pipeline + account mapping (Orbit / Redwood)
messages:
From: Sophie Lambert <sophie@orbitanalytics.com>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Sector sync: overlap between Orbit & Redwood reps on East fintech accounts

Priyom —

Quick note from our side: after our last co-marketing push we’re seeing pipeline duplication across a cluster of East coast fintech targets (notably BlueFin Tech, LedgerWave, and Shoreline Payments). Our AE (Ben) just flagged that two of those are showing active Redwood reps in HubSpot while Orbit has existing SOW conversations. I’ve attached the current Orbit pipeline extract (Orbit_Redwood_Pipeline_Q2.xlsx) so you can see what we’re seeing on our side.

We don’t want to step on each other — can we get a short mapping exercise to resolve account owners and decide co-sell rules for accounts where both teams are engaged? Specific asks: 
- Can you share the Redwood account ownership export for the East fintech segment?
- Are you open to a time-boxed co-sell window for contested accounts (e.g., 30 days) before primary ownership is assigned?

Ben is CC’d — he’s the Orbit lead on these accounts. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week if that helps.

Best,
Sophie Lambert
Head of Partnerships, Orbit Analytics

Subject: Re: Sector sync: overlap between Orbit & Redwood reps on East fintech accounts

Thanks Sophie — and thanks for the export. I’m pulling the Redwood ownership list now and looping in the folks who should own this at Redwood (Marissa / Jonas / Laura). Agree we should avoid duplicate outreach. 

A few quick proposals from my side:
- Share a single canonical mapping (CSV) that marks primary / contesting / referral for each account.
- For accounts with active SOW or legal already underway, default to the partner that has an executed SOW unless there’s a clear product dependency.
- Implement a 21–30 day co-sell buffer where both parties can pursue, and at the end of the buffer the canonical owner is recorded and the other party gets a defined referral credit (or pipe handoff).

Can Marissa/Laura/Jonas weigh in on contested accounts (BlueFin, LedgerWave, Shoreline)? I’ve added a short note file with my suggested rules. If everyone agrees, I’ll merge the mapping into HubSpot and propose the MoU language for the referral/cutover.

—Priyom
Priyom Das

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sophie Lambert <sophie@orbitanalytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sector sync: overlap between Orbit & Redwood reps on East fintech accounts

Appreciate the heads-up, Sophie. A couple of practical constraints from the Redwood AE side: we have two active opportunities with likely close dates in Q2 where Redwood is the incumbent technology decision (one is BlueFin — ARR ~ $420k). If we suddenly de-prioritize those, we risk delivery and churn implications. 

Suggested short-term operating model:
1) For the 3 contested accounts listed, enable a 21-day joint-engagement window (both teams can advance).
2) If no executed commercial agreement by day 21, the partner who brought the SOW or has the deeper integration work will be assigned primary ownership.
3) At assignment time, the non-owner receives a 12% referral credit on any new SaaS commit (we can record this in HubSpot).
4) Build a single source CSV (zone_account_map_v1.csv) that includes: account, current pipeline stage, current owner, partner contacts, last-touch date, contested-flag, recommended-action.

I’ll draft the CSV and drop in the first pass — Jonas, Laura: please flag anything that would prevent us from moving forward on that 21-day window for BlueFin. Also want to be explicit about support handoff and who owns the technical PoC.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Alliances | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks — I’ve created the first-pass CSV and attached it (zone_account_map_v1.csv). The file contains an ownership recommendation column with our suggested primary owner per account based on last-touch, contract status, and product fit. Quick notes:
- BlueFin Tech: Redwood shows an active implementation contract (signed LOI) and a proof-of-concept underway with our infra team. Recommend Redwood primary, Orbit referral.
- LedgerWave: no legal yet, Orbit has earlier SOW discussions — recommend partner primary, Redwood referral.
- Shoreline Payments: contested. Suggest joint AE cadence for 21 days and then evaluate.

Sophie / Ben — take a look at the CSV and add any metadata we missed (legal status, partner SOW refs). If you’re ok, let’s get a short MoU that codifies the 21-day co-sell window + referral % (Marissa suggested 12%). I’m free Thursday morning for a 30-min sync.

Regards,
